The gist of the prosecution case is that the accused No.1 and 2 knowing the fact that one acre 06 guntas of land in Sy.No.33/2 of Avalahalli village in Bengaluru North Tq., is acquired by the BDA, Bengaluru on 27-03-1981 have with common intention to make wrongful gain concealing the fact of acquisition of land and made CW-1 to CW-5 to believe that the accused were owners of the said land and entered into an agreement of sale for total consideration of Rs.1,17,60,000/- and subsequently the accused No.1 and 2 received sum of Rs.22 Lakhs from CW1, Rs.22 lakhs from CW-2, Rs.18 lakhs from CW-3 Rs.20 lakhs from CW-4 and Rs.26 lakhs from CW-5 in all the accused No.1 and 2 have received Rs.1,00,00,000/- (One crore) from CW 1 to 5 as advance and executed agreement of sale deed in favour of  3  C.C.No.1385/2016 CW 1 to 5.

Further when CW 1 to 5 came to know that the said property belongs to BDA, and asked the accused No.1 and 2 about their misdeed, A-1 and A-2 in furtherance of their common intention, criminally intimidated to the lives of CW 1 to 5 that they should not come to their house and should not ask for repayment of money and thus accused have cheated CW 1 to 5.
Based on the said first information, a case in Crime No.249/2014 came to be registered against the Accused for the aforesaid offences.

sentences.text:
My finding to the above points are as under:-
 Point No.1.......In the Negative.
 Point No.2.......As per final Order, for the following :-
 REASONS  9.
POINT No.1:-
It is the fundamental principle of criminal jurisprudence that the prosecution will have to establish its case beyond all reasonable doubt.
In order to prove the same, the prosecution has examined five witnesses as PW1 to 5 and got marked Ex,P.1 and Ex.P2 documents.
10. CW3 was examined as PW1.
She in her chief examination has deposed that Accused No.2 had executed agreement of sale in her favour and in the favour of CW1, 2, 4 and 5.

She has also deposed that they had paid Rs.1,00,00,000/- to the R Kiran vs Mala on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199512488/
4 Accused No.1.
However, the accused have not given sites to them and cheated them.
She deposed that in order to repay the said amount accused No.1 issued cheques to them all of which came to  6  C.C.No.1385/2016 be dishonored as account closed.
On 20-11-2014 when they went to the house of the accused, the Accused No.2 threatened them.
During her cross examination, she has deposed that the agreement was not registered or notarized.
She has stated that in the agreement, accused No.2 had not signed.
She admits that CW-2 is her husband and CW-1 is her brother in law.
She also admits that Sandhya is wife of CW-1 and CW-5 is their family friend.
She states that she does not know whether the stamp purchased for the purpose of Loan agreement.
She has deposed that they had paid Rs.One Crore by way of cash to accused No.1.
She has deposed that in the year, 2014 they had demanded the amount back.
She has deposed that the accused had given four cheques to them.
She has deposed that they have filed C.C.No.30283/2014 in respect of the dishonored cheques.
She admits that on 10-11-2020 the case came to be dismissed.
11. CW-4 was examined PW-4, CW-5 was examined as PW-3 and CW-1 was examined as PW-4.
They had never turned before the court for further cross examination.
Hence, their evidence was discarded and they were dropped.
7  C.C.No.1385/2016  12. CW-2 was examined as PW-5.

He has deposed that accused No.1 and 2 had taken money from him and others R Kiran vs Mala on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199512488/
5 promising to give sites.
However, their property was already acquired by BDA.
When he demanded the money back, the accused gave cheque to him which came to be dishonored.
13. The above being the evidence on record, it would be appropriate to see whether prosecution can bring the guilt of the accused on record or not.
14. In this case, it is alleged that accused had entered into agreement of sale with CW-1 to 5 and received Rs.One Crore as advance amount.
To prove the same, the prosecution has failed to produce the sale agreement in order to show the transaction.
When the entire case of the prosecution is based upon agreement of sale between the accused CW 1 to 5, the non production of the alleged sale agreement is fatal to the case of prosecution.
15 . It is the case of prosecution that CW 1 to 5 had paid Rs.One crore as advance amount.
PW-1 during her cross examination states that they had paid the entire amount in cash.
This is very hard to believe as no common person would pay cash of Rs.One crore towards sale agreement.
Hence, this aspect also creates doubt in the mind of this court.
16 . It is the case of the prosecution that the land in which Sites were offered for sale was already acquired by BDA.

Even to prove this aspect the prosecution has failed to produce any R Kiran vs Mala on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199512488/
6 Notification to show the lands were acquired by BDA even before the alleged transaction.
Hence, this also creates doubt in the mind of this court.
17. Going by all the above discussion, this court holds that the prosecution has failed to prove the transaction and the payment of amount by CW 1 to 5 to the Accused No.1.
Hence this court extends benefit of doubt to the accused and holds that the prosecution has failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt.
Accordingly I answer point No.1 in the Negative.
18. POINT No.2:- In the result, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER In exercise of power conferred U/s.248(1) of Cr.P.C., accused No.1 and 2 are acquitted of the C.C.No.1385/2016 offences punishable U/s.420, 504 r/w/s 34 of IPC.
The bail bond and surety bonds executed by the accused No.1 and 2 shall remain in force for 6 months.
